title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck sets up the analytic description of the moduli stack of elliptic curves as a basic model for the 'Teichmüller tower' programme.

(1) The space PD = {(z1,z2) ∈ C^2 : ratio in the upper half plane D} is identified with Hom^+(Z^2, C), the oriented embeddings of Z^2 as a lattice. Equivalently, it parametrises elliptic curves C/(Z z1 + Z z2) together with a symplectic basis of H_1 (φ(e1,e2) = +1) and the differential dz. Over PM_{1,1} (pairs (E, ω), ω a nonzero invariant differential, i.e. the C^*-torsor of the Hodge bundle over M_{1,1}) this gives a cartesian square:
- top row: PD → PM_{1,1};
- bottom row: D → M_{1,1};
- vertical maps: the projective map (z1,z2) ↦ ratio, and the forgetful map PM_{1,1} → M_{1,1}.
The map D → M_{1,1} is 'Galois' with group SL(2,Z), and D ≅ M̃_{1,1} is the strict Torelli rigidification (an oriented symplectic basis, with e2/e1 = τ ∈ D).

(2) C^* × SL(2,Z) acts on PD by (z1,z2) ↦ λ(a z1 + b z2, c z1 + d z2). Passing to the quotient by C^* gives the SL(2,Z) action on D. This is the restriction of the natural GL(2,R) Möbius action on P^1(C); SL(2,R) preserves D, and Aut_C(D) = PSL(2,R) (written loosely as SL(2,R)).

(3) Boxed conclusions, as orbifolds/analytic stacks: M^an_{1,1} ≅ [D/SL(2,Z)] and PM^an_{1,1} ≅ [PD/SL(2,Z)]. Variants with GL(2,Z): to make det −1 elements act on D one composes with complex conjugation. He writes u_g = τ^{α(g)}·g, with τ here denoting complex conjugation and α(g) ∈ Z/2 equal to 1 iff det g = −1. This gives the 'real' or dianalytic moduli stacks, where anti-holomorphic isomorphisms are allowed.

(4) The Teichmüller modular group is T_{11} ≅ SL(2,Z). The 'special' version ST_{11} ≅ the preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R). This is the braid group B_3, the fundamental group of the C^*-bundle PM_{1,1} (or its universal cover D×C, see next page).

Purpose: a worked base case (g,ν) = (1,1) for the Teichmüller tower / Galois action programme of the Esquisse, including the central extension and the complex-conjugation (Gal(C/R)) twist.
errors: Convention inconsistency: the header defines PD via z1/z2 ∈ D, but the vertical map is written (z1,z2) ↦ z2/z1, with e2/e1 = τ. With the action (z1,z2) ↦ (a z1 + b z2, c z1 + d z2), the formula (aτ+b)/(cτ+d) holds for τ = z1/z2, not z2/z1. The crossed-out (dz+c)/(bz+a) shows he noticed this, and the next page uses the section τ ↦ (τ,1), i.e. τ = z1/z2.
'SL(2,R) ≅ Aut_C(D)' should be PSL(2,R) (the kernel ±1 acts trivially on D).
The symbol τ is overloaded: e2/e1 = τ ∈ D in one place, complex conjugation in u_g = τ^{α(g)} g in another.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook material, written out as a base case for the Teichmüller tower. The only mildly characteristic touches are the systematic inclusion of the C^*-torsor PM_{1,1}, the central extension ST_{11}, and the complex-conjugation twist for GL(2,Z); all of these are well known.
transcription_corrections: In u_g = τ^{α(g)}·g and in the GL^{±1}(2,R) action formula, τ denotes complex conjugation (written as an exponent on z1, z2), not the period ratio.
The label under the bottom-left arrow reads 'gal. quotient par Sl(2,Z)' (Galois quotient), not 'gal. quo-par[?]'.
The header shows 'Hom^+(Z^2, C)' with a superscript sign that is partly overwritten; the crossed-out text beneath is '≃ D × C^*'.
